name: figma-duplicate-ids-scorebug
exporter: Figma - Export > SVG, Include "id" attribute ON, Outline text OFF
story: A scorebug built by drawing the home side and duplicating the group for the away side, so both halves keep the same layer names and Figma writes each one into id verbatim.
idioms: id="Score", id="Team", id="Side" and id="Score plate" each appearing TWICE in one document - Figma writes a layer name into id without uniquifying it, and a duplicated group keeps its names
no data-name, no serif:id, no inkscape:label anywhere - unlike Illustrator and Affinity, Figma has no second attribute holding the original spelling, so the duplicate id is all there is
the two scores centre-anchored (text-anchor="middle") over their own plates while one team name is start-anchored and the other end-anchored - the shape a symmetrical bug always takes
a numeric sample on both score layers (3 and 2), which §3 says proposes a number field
layer names with spaces written straight into id (id="Bug plate", id="Score plate")
no XML declaration, zero indentation, fill="none" on the root, uppercase hex, fill="white" as a keyword, fill-opacity for layer alpha
xml:space="preserve" plus style="white-space: pre" on every text, letter-spacing in em, fractional baselines
whyThisMatters: The scoreboard is the other graphic the 2026-09-12 production is decided by, and duplicating one side to make the other is how every scoreboard on earth is drawn - so repeated ids are the NORMAL case for this shape, not a corner. An SVG tolerates them; an HTML document does not, and the artwork is inlined into one, where getElementById answers with whichever element came first. The corpus proved the repeat-numbering promise only through Illustrator, which uniquifies the id itself and keeps the real spelling in data-name - so the rule had never been tested on a file where the duplicate is all there is. Four fields where an operator can raise either score independently is the whole product here; three fields, or two that write to the same digit, is a scoreboard that cannot keep score.
